Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the rejected transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reject counter (WS-REJECT-COUNT) is incremented by 1; the original transaction data (DALYTRAN-RECORD) is moved to the reject record data area (REJECT-TRAN-DATA); the validation failure reason code and description (WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER) are appended as a trailer (VALIDATION-TRAILER); the complete reject record is written to the Daily Rejects File (DALYREJS-FILE); the program then loops back to read the next transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Rejected Transaction to Daily Rejects File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction fails any validation check, the original transaction data along with the validation failure reason code and description are written to the Daily Rejects File for review and remediation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares the transaction record for writing to the Transaction Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following fields are mapped from the daily transaction record to the transaction master record: Transaction ID (DALYTRAN-ID to TRAN-ID), Transaction Type Code (DALYTRAN-TYPE-CD to TRAN-TYPE-CD), Transaction Category Code (DALYTRAN-CAT-CD to TRAN-CAT-CD), Transaction Source (DALYTRAN-SOURCE to TRAN-SOURCE), Transaction Description (DALYTRAN-DESC to TRAN-DESC), Transaction Amount (DALYTRAN-AMT to TRAN-AMT), Merchant ID (DALYTRAN-MERCHANT-ID to TRAN-MERCHANT-ID), Merchant Name (DALYTRAN-MERCHANT-NAME to TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME), Merchant City (DALYTRAN-MERCHANT-CITY to TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY), Merchant ZIP (DALYTRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP to TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP), Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM to TRAN-CARD-NUM), and Original Timestamp (DALYTRAN-ORIG-TS to TRAN-ORIG-TS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Transaction Record for Posting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before a validated transaction can be written to the Transaction Master File, all relevant fields from the daily transaction record must be mapped to the transaction master record structure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A validated transaction is being prepared for posting to the Transaction Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program generates the processing timestamp by calling the Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time is captured and formatted into a standard timestamp (DB2-FORMAT-TS) containing year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds separated by standard delimiters (dashes and dots); this formatted timestamp is stored as the transaction processing timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS) on the transaction master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Generate Processing Timestamp for Posted Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each posted transaction must be stamped with the date and time it was processed by the system. The current system date and time is captured and formatted into a standard timestamp format for recording on the transaction master record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A validated transaction is being posted and the Transaction Category Balance File (TCATBAL-FILE) is open for read/write access
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program looks up the Transaction Category Balance record using the composite key of Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID), Transaction Type Code (DALYTRAN-TYPE-CD), and Transaction Category Code (DALYTRAN-CAT-CD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a matching record is NOT found, a new Transaction Category Balance record must be created; if a matching record IS found, the existing record must be updated by adding the transaction amount to the existing balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Category Balance Lookup and Create-or-Update Decision
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system maintains a running balance for each unique combination of Account, Transaction Type, and Transaction Category. Before updating, the system checks whether a balance record already exists for this combination to determine whether to create a new record or update an existing one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup of the Transaction Category Balance File found no existing record for the combination of Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID), Transaction Type Code (DALYTRAN-TYPE-CD), and Transaction Category Code (DALYTRAN-CAT-CD)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program creates a new Transaction Category Balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new record is initialized with all fields cleared; the Account ID is set to XREF-ACCT-ID; the Transaction Type Code is set to DALYTRAN-TYPE-CD; the Transaction Category Code is set to DALYTRAN-CAT-CD; the category balance (TRAN-CAT-BAL) is set by adding DALYTRAN-AMT to the initialized zero balance; the new record is written to the Transaction Category Balance File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Create New Transaction Category Balance Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Transaction Category Balance record exists for a given Account, Transaction Type, and Category combination, a new record is created and initialized with the current transaction amount as the opening balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Category Balance record was found for the combination of Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program updates the existing Transaction Category Balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is added to the existing category balance (TRAN-CAT-BAL), and the updated record is rewritten to the Transaction Category Balance File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Existing Transaction Category Balance Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Category Balance record already exists for the Account, Transaction Type, and Category combination, the transaction amount is added to the existing running balance and the record is updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has passed all validations and the account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) has been retrieved from the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program updates the account balances
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) regardless of the sign of the amount

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Account Current Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every posted transaction, regardless of whether it is a credit or debit, must be applied to the account's overall current balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account's current balance has been updated with the transaction amount and the transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is known
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the sign of the transaction amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If DALYTRAN-AMT is greater than or equal to 0 (positive or zero), it is classified as a credit and DALYTRAN-AMT is added to the current cycle credit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT); if DALYTRAN-AMT is less than 0 (negative), it is classified as a debit and DALYTRAN-AMT is added to the current cycle debit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT); the updated account record is then saved back to the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify Transaction as Credit or Debit for Cycle Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: In addition to updating the overall account balance, each transaction must be classified as either a credit or a debit based on the sign of the transaction amount, and the appropriate cycle-level running total must be updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record (TRAN-RECORD) has been fully populated with all transaction fields and the processing timestamp, and all account and category balance updates have been successfully applied
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the transaction record to the Transaction Master File (TRANSACT-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete transaction record is written to the Transaction Master File; the program then loops back to read the next transaction from the Daily Transaction File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Posted Transaction to Transaction Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all account and category balance updates are complete, the fully populated transaction record including the processing timestamp is written to the Transaction Master File as the permanent record of the posted transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All records in the Daily Transaction File have been processed (end-of-file reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes its processing loop and performs end-of-job activities
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All six files are closed; the total number of transactions processed (WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT) is displayed; the total number of transactions rejected (WS-REJECT-COUNT) is displayed; if WS-REJECT-COUNT is greater than 0, the return code is set to 4 to signal that rejected transactions exist and require attention; if WS-REJECT-COUNT equals 0, no special return code is set and the program ends normally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion Reporting and Return Code Setting
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the end of processing, the program closes all files, displays a summary of transactions processed and rejected, and signals downstream processes if any rejections occurred by setting a return code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The daily transaction processing program is starting execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes and prepares to process transactions
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must open all six files in the following strict sequence before processing any transaction: (1) Daily Transaction File, (2) Transaction Master File, (3) Card-to-Account Cross Reference File, (4) Daily Rejects File, (5) Account Master File, (6) Transaction Category Balance File. Only after all six files are successfully opened is the program ready to begin transaction processing.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential File Initialization Order for Transaction Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: All six required files must be opened in a mandatory sequence before any daily transaction processing can begin. The order is: Daily Transaction input file, Transaction Master output file, Card-to-Account Cross Reference file, Daily Rejects output file, Account Master file, and Transaction Category Balance file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is initializing and the Daily Transaction File is the first file to be opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Daily Transaction File as a read-only input source
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Transaction Master File). If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately stops all processing and terminates with an error indicating the Daily Transaction File could not be opened.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Daily Transaction File Must Be Available for Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Daily Transaction File is the source of all transactions to be processed. It must be successfully opened for reading before any processing begins. If it cannot be opened, all processing must stop immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File has been successfully opened and the program is proceeding to open the Transaction Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Master File as a write-only output destination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Card-to-Account Cross Reference File). If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately stops all processing and terminates with an error indicating the Transaction Master File could not be opened.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Master Output File Must Be Available for Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Master File is the destination for all successfully validated and posted transactions. It must be successfully opened for writing before any processing begins. If it cannot be opened, all processing must stop immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File and Transaction Master File have been successfully opened and the program is proceeding to open the Card-to-Account Cross Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Card-to-Account Cross Reference File as a read-only input source
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Daily Rejects File). If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately stops all processing and terminates with an error indicating the Card-to-Account Cross Reference File could not be opened.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card-to-Account Cross Reference File Must Be Available for Card Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card-to-Account Cross Reference File is required to validate card numbers and retrieve the associated account identifiers during transaction processing. It must be successfully opened for reading before any processing begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File, Transaction Master File, and Card-to-Account Cross Reference File have been successfully opened and the program is proceeding to open the Daily Rejects File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Daily Rejects File as a write-only output destination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Account Master File). If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately stops all processing and terminates with an error indicating the Daily Rejects File could not be opened.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Daily Rejects Output File Must Be Available for Recording Invalid Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Daily Rejects File is the destination for all transactions that fail validation. It must be successfully opened for writing before any processing begins, ensuring that any rejected transaction can be recorded with its failure reason.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File, Transaction Master File, Card-to-Account Cross Reference File, and Daily Rejects File have been successfully opened and the program is proceeding to open the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account Master File for both reading and updating (read/write access)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the next required file (Transaction Category Balance File). If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately stops all processing and terminates with an error indicating the Account Master File could not be opened.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Must Be Available for Account Lookup and Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Master File is required both to validate account details during transaction validation (credit limit, expiration date) and to update account balances when transactions are posted. It must be opened for both reading and updating before any processing begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All five preceding files (Daily Transaction, Transaction Master, Card-to-Account Cross Reference, Daily Rejects, and Account Master) have been successfully opened and the program is proceeding to open the Transaction Category Balance File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction Category Balance File for both reading and updating (read/write access)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opens successfully, all six required files are now open and the program is ready to begin processing daily transactions. If the file cannot be opened for any reason, the program immediately stops all processing and terminates with an error indicating the Transaction Category Balance File could not be opened.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Category Balance File Must Be Available for Balance Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Category Balance File maintains running balance totals by account, transaction type, and transaction category. It must be opened for both reading and updating before any processing begins, as it is updated for every successfully posted transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the initialization phase and is attempting to open the required files in sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any one of the six required files (Daily Transaction File, Transaction Master File, Card-to-Account Cross Reference File, Daily Rejects File, Account Master File, or Transaction Category Balance File) fails to open successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must immediately stop all processing without reading or processing any transactions. The program terminates with a critical error condition, ensuring no partial or incomplete processing occurs.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Any File Unavailability Prevents All Transaction Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: If any one of the six required files cannot be opened during initialization, the entire transaction processing run must be stopped immediately. No transactions can be processed unless all required files are available, ensuring data integrity across the entire processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is initializing and opening the six required files
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Each file is opened according to its business function
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following access modes must be enforced based on business purpose: (1) Daily Transaction File — opened as INPUT only, as it is the source of transactions to be processed and must not be modified; (2) Transaction Master File — opened as OUTPUT only, as it receives newly posted transaction records; (3) Card-to-Account Cross Reference File — opened as INPUT only, as it is a reference lookup file and must not be modified; (4) Daily Rejects File — opened as OUTPUT only, as it receives rejected transaction records; (5) Account Master File — opened for both READ and UPDATE, as accounts are looked up for validation and then updated with new balances; (6) Transaction Category Balance File — opened for both READ and UPDATE, as category balances are looked up and then updated with transaction amounts.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Business Purpose Determines File Access Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each file is opened with an access mode that reflects its specific business role in the transaction processing cycle. Source files are read-only, destination files are write-only, and files that require both lookup and update are opened for read/write access.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction file is open and the processing loop is active with End-of-File flag set to 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to read the next sequential record from the Daily Transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next transaction record is read into the Daily Transaction Record buffer and made available for subsequent validation and posting steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Read of Daily Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each iteration of the processing loop reads the next available transaction record sequentially from the Daily Transaction file to make it available for validation and posting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction file is open and a read operation has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns a 'No More Records' condition indicating there are no further transactions to process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', the processing loop is stopped, and the program proceeds to close all files and produce summary reports

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection on Daily Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no more transaction records are available in the Daily Transaction file, the processing loop must be terminated and the program must proceed to file closure and summary reporting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed against the Daily Transaction file and the End-of-File flag remains 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A transaction record is successfully read and is available for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total transaction counter (WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT) is incremented by 1, reflecting that one additional transaction has been received for processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Counter Increment on Successful Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every transaction record successfully retrieved from the Daily Transaction file must be counted to maintain an accurate total of transactions processed during the run, which is reported at end-of-job.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been successfully read and is ready for validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Validation Failure Reason Code must be set to zero, indicating a clean, passing state with no prior failure recorded for this transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Validation Failure Reason Code Before Transaction Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating each daily transaction, the validation failure reason code must be reset to zero to ensure no residual failure state from a previously processed transaction influences the current transaction's validation outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Validation Failure Reason Code has been reset to zero for the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues preparing to validate the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Validation Failure Reason Description must be cleared to blank spaces, ensuring no prior failure description text is associated with the current transaction before validation begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Validation Failure Reason Description Before Transaction Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating each daily transaction, the validation failure reason description must be cleared to blank spaces to ensure no residual failure message from a previously processed transaction carries over into the current transaction's validation result.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read from the Daily Transaction file and contains a card number field (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the transaction by initiating a card number lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number from the daily transaction record is set as the search key (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM) to be used for the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Card Number from Daily Transaction for Cross Reference Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card number present on the incoming daily transaction record must be extracted and used as the key to search the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number from the daily transaction record has been extracted and set as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file using the card number as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Cross Reference record if the card number exists, or identifies the card as not found if no matching record exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lookup Card Number in Card-to-Account Cross Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must perform a direct key-based lookup of the transaction's card number in the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file (XREF-FILE) to determine whether the card is recognized.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read and its card number has been used to search the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number is NOT found in the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file (INVALID KEY condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction validation fail reason is set to 100 and the validation failure description is set to 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND', marking the transaction as invalid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Card Number — Mark Transaction as Failed with Reason Code 100
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the card number on the transaction does not exist in the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file, the transaction must be marked as invalid with a specific reason code and description to indicate an unrecognized card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read and its card number has been used to search the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number IS found in the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file (NOT INVALID KEY condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross Reference record is successfully retrieved, making the associated Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) available for the next validation step, and the validation fail reason remains 0 (no failure)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Card Number — Retrieve Associated Account ID from Cross Reference Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card number is successfully found in the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file, the associated Account ID must be retrieved from the cross reference record for use in subsequent account-level validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number lookup against the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file has been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation fail reason is NOT equal to 0 (i.e., card validation has failed with reason code 100)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account lookup validation step (1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT) is skipped entirely, and the transaction proceeds directly to rejection processing with the existing failure reason and description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Account Validation When Card Validation Has Failed
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the card number validation step has failed (reason code is not zero), the system must not proceed to the account-level validation step. Further validation is only performed when all prior validation steps have passed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed card number validation and a valid Card Cross-Reference record has been retrieved containing the associated Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the account existence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference record is used as the lookup key to search the Account Master file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account ID from Card Cross-Reference for Account Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before looking up the account in the Account Master file, the system must retrieve the Account ID that was resolved from the Card Cross-Reference file during the card validation step. This Account ID is used as the key to locate the corresponding account record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed card number validation and the Account ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system looks up the Account Master file using the retrieved Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines whether a matching account record exists in the Account Master file and routes the transaction accordingly — either flagging it as invalid or proceeding with further validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Must Exist in Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must verify that the Account ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file corresponds to an existing account record in the Account Master file. This ensures that only transactions linked to valid, existing accounts are processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed card number validation and the Account ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system looks up the Account Master file using the Account ID and no matching account record is found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction is marked as invalid with Validation Failure Reason Code 101 and Failure Description 'ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND', and no further validation steps are performed for this transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Transaction as Invalid When Account Record is Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference does not match any record in the Account Master file, the transaction must be marked as invalid. The transaction is assigned a specific failure reason code and description to indicate that the account could not be found, preventing the transaction from being posted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed card number validation and the Account ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system looks up the Account Master file using the Account ID and a matching account record is found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account details including current cycle credits, current cycle debits, credit limit, and account expiration date are retrieved and made available, and the transaction proceeds to the credit limit and account expiration date validation checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Further Validation When Account Record is Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account record is successfully located in the Account Master file, the account details become available for subsequent business validations such as credit limit checks and account expiration checks. The transaction remains eligible for posting and proceeds through the remaining validation steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed card number validation and the associated account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file, with values available for Current Cycle Credits, Current Cycle Debits, and the Transaction Amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the projected balance for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Temporary Projected Balance must be computed as: Temporary Balance = Current Cycle Credits minus Current Cycle Debits plus Transaction Amount

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Projected Transaction Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before checking the credit limit, a projected balance is computed for the account by combining the current billing cycle's credits, debits, and the incoming transaction amount. This projected balance represents what the account balance would be if the transaction were approved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed card number validation, the associated account record has been retrieved from the Account Master file, and the Temporary Projected Balance has been calculated as Current Cycle Credits minus Current Cycle Debits plus Transaction Amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Account Credit Limit against the Temporary Projected Balance
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Credit Limit is greater than or equal to the Temporary Projected Balance, the credit limit check passes and processing continues to the next validation; If the Account Credit Limit is less than the Temporary Projected Balance, the transaction is marked as invalid with Validation Fail Reason Code 102 and Validation Fail Reason Description set to 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION', and the transaction is subsequently rejected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Transaction Against Account Credit Limit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After computing the projected balance, the system enforces the account's credit limit policy by comparing the projected balance against the account's approved credit limit. If the projected balance exceeds the credit limit, the transaction is flagged as invalid and cannot be posted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed card number and account existence validations, and the account master record has been successfully retrieved containing the Account Expiration Date, and the transaction record contains a Transaction Origination Date (first 10 characters of the origination timestamp representing the date portion)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Account Expiration Date from the Account Master file against the Transaction Origination Date (date portion only, first 10 characters) from the daily transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Expiration Date is greater than or equal to the Transaction Origination Date, the transaction date falls within the account's valid period and the transaction continues to be considered valid with no change to the validation fail reason; OR if the Account Expiration Date is less than the Transaction Origination Date (account expired before the transaction was made), the transaction is marked as invalid by setting the Validation Fail Reason Code to 103 and the Validation Fail Reason Description to 'TRANSACTION RECEIVED AFTER ACCT EXPIRATION', and the transaction is subsequently flagged for rejection and written to the Daily Rejects file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Expiration Date Validation Against Transaction Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: This rule ensures that a credit card transaction is only accepted if the associated account is still active (not expired) on the date the transaction originated. If the account expiration date is earlier than the transaction origination date, the transaction is flagged as invalid and marked for rejection with a specific reason code and description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has been read and processed through all applicable validation checks, and at least one validation rule has failed resulting in a non-zero Validation Fail Reason code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the Validation Fail Reason is not equal to zero, indicating the transaction did not pass all validations
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Reject Counter (WS-REJECT-COUNT) must be incremented by exactly 1 to reflect the additional rejected transaction in the running total

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Reject Counter on Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a daily transaction fails any validation check, the system must increment the running total of rejected transactions by one before any rejection record is written.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has failed validation and the reject counter has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the rejection record for writing to the Daily Rejects output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire original transaction record (DALYTRAN-RECORD) must be copied verbatim into the transaction data portion (REJECT-TRAN-DATA) of the reject record, preserving all original transaction fields without modification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Original Transaction Data to Reject Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The complete and unmodified original transaction data from the daily transaction input must be preserved in its entirety as the primary data payload of the rejection record, ensuring full traceability of the rejected transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The original transaction data has been copied to the reject record, and the Validation Fail Reason code (WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON) is set to one of the following values: 100 (Invalid Card Number Found), 101 (Account Record Not Found), 102 (Overlimit Transaction), or 103 (Transaction Received After Account Expiration)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the reject record before writing it to the Daily Rejects output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation trailer (WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER) containing both the numeric Validation Fail Reason code and the corresponding Validation Fail Reason Description text must be moved into the VALIDATION-TRAILER field of the reject record, so that the complete reject record contains both the original transaction data and the specific reason for rejection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attach Validation Failure Details to Reject Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The rejection record must include the specific reason why the transaction was rejected by attaching the validation failure reason code and its human-readable description as a trailer to the reject record, enabling downstream review and remediation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reject record (FD-REJS-RECORD) has been fully assembled containing the original transaction data in REJECT-TRAN-DATA and the validation failure reason code and description in VALIDATION-TRAILER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the complete reject record from REJECT-RECORD to the Daily Rejects output file (DALYREJS-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete reject record must be successfully written to the Daily Rejects output file, and processing must return to the main loop to read the next daily transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Complete Reject Record to Daily Rejects Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the reject record is fully assembled with the original transaction data and the validation failure details, the complete record must be written to the Daily Rejects output file to ensure all rejected transactions are captured for downstream review and reprocessing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Transaction ID field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Transaction ID to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Transaction ID from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to uniquely identify the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Transaction Type Code field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Transaction Type Code to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Transaction Type Code from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to classify the type of transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Code from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Transaction Category Code field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Transaction Category Code to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Transaction Category Code from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to classify the spending category of the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Source from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Transaction Source field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Transaction Source to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Transaction Source from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to identify the originating channel or system of the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Description from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Transaction Description field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Transaction Description to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Transaction Description from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to provide a human-readable description of the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Transaction Amount field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Transaction Amount to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Transaction Amount from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to record the monetary value of the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant ID from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Merchant ID field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Merchant ID to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Merchant ID from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to identify the merchant where the transaction occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant Name from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Merchant Name field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Merchant Name to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Merchant Name from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to record the name of the merchant where the transaction occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant City from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Merchant City field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Merchant City to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Merchant City from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to record the city location of the merchant where the transaction occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant ZIP Code from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Merchant ZIP Code field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Merchant ZIP Code to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Merchant ZIP Code from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to record the postal location of the merchant where the transaction occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Card Number field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Card Number to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Card Number from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to associate the transaction with the cardholder's account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction master record for posting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Origination Timestamp from the daily transaction record is mapped to the Origination Timestamp field of the master transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Origination Timestamp to Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing a validated transaction for posting, the Origination Timestamp from the daily transaction input record must be carried forward to the master transaction record to preserve the original date and time when the transaction was initiated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has passed all validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the mapping of all fields from the daily transaction record to the master transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The master transaction record is fully populated with Transaction ID, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Source, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant ZIP Code, Card Number, and Origination Timestamp, and the record is ready for the downstream posting steps: Transaction Category Balance update, Account Master update, and Transaction File write

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fully Populate Transaction Master Record Before Posting
all_rules.Rule_Description: All transaction fields — Transaction ID, Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant ZIP, Card Number, and Origination Timestamp — must be completely mapped from the daily transaction record to the master transaction record before any downstream posting steps (category balance update, account update, transaction file write) are executed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid transaction has passed all business validations and is ready to be posted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the generation of a processing timestamp for the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the current system date and time from the system clock and stores it in the working timestamp field (COBOL-TS) to be used as the basis for the final formatted processing timestamp

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current System Date and Time for Transaction Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When generating a processing timestamp, the system must capture the current system date and time as the authoritative source for recording when a transaction was processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date and time has been captured into the working timestamp field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts individual date and time components from the captured system timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then:
The following components are individually extracted and stored in their respective fields:
- 4-digit Year (YYYY) extracted into DB2-YYYY
- 2-digit Month (MM) extracted into DB2-MM
- 2-digit Day (DD) extracted into DB2-DD
- 2-digit Hour (HH) extracted into DB2-HH
- 2-digit Minute (MM) extracted into DB2-MIN
- 2-digit Second (SS) extracted into DB2-SS
- 3-digit Milliseconds (mmm) extracted into DB2-MIL

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Individual Date and Time Components from System Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: The captured system date and time must be decomposed into its individual components — Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, and Milliseconds — so that each part can be independently assembled into the required standard timestamp format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date and time components including milliseconds have been extracted from the system timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system pads the remaining sub-millisecond precision portion of the timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The remaining precision field (DB2-REST) is set to '0000', representing four trailing zeros that complete the timestamp to the required precision level of YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmm0000

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pad Remaining Timestamp Precision with Zeros
all_rules.Rule_Description: The standard timestamp format requires precision beyond milliseconds. Since the system clock does not provide sub-millisecond precision, the remaining four digits of the timestamp must be padded with zeros to complete the required format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All individual date components (Year, Month, Day), time components (Hour, Minute, Second, Milliseconds), and the zero-padded precision field have been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the final timestamp string by inserting separator characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then:
The following separators are applied to produce the final timestamp:
- Three dash characters ('-') are placed as DB2-STREEP-1, DB2-STREEP-2, and DB2-STREEP-3 to separate the date and date-time boundary portions
- Three dot characters ('.') are placed as DB2-DOT-1, DB2-DOT-2, and DB2-DOT-3 to separate the time components
- The resulting assembled timestamp conforms to the format: YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmm0000

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assemble Final Timestamp Using Standard Date and Time Separators
all_rules.Rule_Description: The individual date and time components must be assembled into a single standard-format timestamp string using the prescribed separator characters: dashes (-) between date components and dots (.) between time components, producing the format YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmm0000.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The processing timestamp has been fully assembled in the standard format YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmm0000 and stored in the formatted timestamp field (DB2-FORMAT-TS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the formatted timestamp onto the transaction record being posted
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fully formatted processing timestamp (DB2-FORMAT-TS) is moved into the Transaction Processing Timestamp field (TRAN-PROC-TS) on the transaction record, permanently recording the date and time at which the transaction was processed and posted to the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Formatted Timestamp as Transaction Processing Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the processing timestamp has been fully assembled and formatted, it must be stored as the official Transaction Processing Timestamp on the transaction record to permanently record the exact date and time the transaction was posted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid daily transaction has passed all validation checks and is ready to be posted, and the Account ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the Transaction Category Balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must build a composite lookup key consisting of: (1) Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference record, (2) Transaction Type Code from the daily transaction, and (3) Transaction Category Code from the daily transaction — all three values combined form the unique key used to identify the correct Transaction Category Balance record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Composite Lookup Key for Transaction Category Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before looking up or updating a transaction category balance record, a composite key must be constructed from three data elements: the Account ID (derived from the card cross-reference), the Transaction Type Code, and the Transaction Category Code from the daily transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The composite key has been built using Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup against the Transaction Category Balance file using the composite key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the matching Transaction Category Balance record if it exists; if no matching record is found, the system flags that a new record needs to be created (internal flag set to 'Y'); if the record is found, the flag remains 'N' indicating an update is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lookup Transaction Category Balance Record by Composite Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must attempt to retrieve an existing Transaction Category Balance record from the Transaction Category Balance file using the composite key of Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup has been performed against the Transaction Category Balance file using the composite key of Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If no matching record was found, the system must proceed to create a new Transaction Category Balance record; if a matching record was found, the system must proceed to update the existing Transaction Category Balance record by adding the transaction amount to the existing balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether to Create or Update Transaction Category Balance Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Based on the result of the Transaction Category Balance file lookup, the system must decide whether to create a new category balance record or update the existing one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No Transaction Category Balance record exists for the combination of Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system creates a new Transaction Category Balance record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) initialize the new record to clear any residual data, (2) set the Account ID to the value from the Card Cross-Reference record, (3) set the Transaction Type Code to the value from the daily transaction, (4) set the Transaction Category Code to the value from the daily transaction, and (5) set the category balance by adding the transaction amount to the initialized (zero) balance, resulting in the opening balance equal to the transaction amount

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize New Transaction Category Balance Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no existing Transaction Category Balance record is found for the given composite key, a new record must be created and initialized with the transaction details and the transaction amount as the opening balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Transaction Category Balance record has been initialized with Account ID, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Code, and the transaction amount as the opening balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the new record to the Transaction Category Balance file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new Transaction Category Balance record is permanently stored in the Transaction Category Balance file and is available for future transaction processing against the same Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code combination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write New Transaction Category Balance Record to File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a new Transaction Category Balance record has been initialized with all required fields and the opening balance, it must be permanently written to the Transaction Category Balance file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An existing Transaction Category Balance record has been found and retrieved for the composite key of Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the category balance
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must add the transaction amount from the current daily transaction to the existing category balance value in the retrieved record, producing an updated running total for that account's transaction type and category combination; the transaction amount may be positive or negative

all_rules.Rule_Name: Add Transaction Amount to Existing Category Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an existing Transaction Category Balance record is found, the transaction amount from the current daily transaction must be added to the existing running category balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An existing Transaction Category Balance record has been retrieved and its balance has been updated by adding the current transaction amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system saves the updated record back to the Transaction Category Balance file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Balance file is updated with the new running balance for the Account ID, Transaction Type Code, and Transaction Category Code combination, replacing the previously stored balance value with the newly computed total

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Updated Transaction Category Balance Record to File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been added to the existing category balance, the updated Transaction Category Balance record must be saved back to the Transaction Category Balance file, replacing the previous record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has passed all validations and the Account Master record has been retrieved, containing the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction is being posted to the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is added to the account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), updating it to reflect the new total balance after this transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Account Current Balance with Transaction Amount
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every processed transaction, regardless of whether it is a credit or debit, must be applied to the account's overall current balance by adding the transaction amount directly to it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is available for posting and the account's current cycle credit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) and current cycle debit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) are available in the Account Master record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction amount is evaluated for its sign
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the transaction amount is greater than or equal to zero, it is classified as a credit transaction and routed to update the current cycle credit total; if the transaction amount is less than zero, it is classified as a debit transaction and routed to update the current cycle debit total

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify Transaction as Credit or Debit Based on Amount Sign
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must determine whether a transaction is a credit or a debit by evaluating the sign of the transaction amount, in order to apply it to the correct cycle-level tracking total on the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been classified as a credit transaction because its amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is greater than or equal to zero, and the account's current cycle credit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) is available in the Account Master record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The credit transaction is being posted to the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is added to the account's current cycle credit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT), increasing the cumulative credit amount for the current billing cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Credit Transaction Amount to Current Cycle Credit Total
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is identified as a credit (amount is zero or positive), the transaction amount must be accumulated into the account's current billing cycle credit total to maintain accurate cycle-level credit tracking.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been classified as a debit transaction because its amount (DALYTRAN-AMT) is less than zero, and the account's current cycle debit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) is available in the Account Master record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The debit transaction is being posted to the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction amount (DALYTRAN-AMT), which is a negative value, is added to the account's current cycle debit total (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT), updating the cumulative debit amount for the current billing cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Debit Transaction Amount to Current Cycle Debit Total
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is identified as a debit (amount is negative), the transaction amount must be accumulated into the account's current billing cycle debit total to maintain accurate cycle-level debit tracking.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) and the appropriate cycle total (either ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT or ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) have been updated in the in-memory Account Master record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) following the posting of a transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All balance computations for the transaction have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The updated Account Master record is written back to the Account Master file, permanently saving the new current balance and the updated cycle credit or debit total for the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Persist Updated Account Balances to Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all balance updates have been applied to the account record in memory, the updated account record must be saved back to the Account Master file to ensure all balance changes are permanently recorded and available for future transactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A daily transaction has passed all validations and is ready to be posted, with the following source data available: Transaction ID, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Source, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant ZIP Code, Card Number, and Original Transaction Timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction record for writing to the Transaction Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record must be fully populated by mapping: Transaction ID from the daily transaction, Transaction Type Code from the daily transaction, Transaction Category Code from the daily transaction, Transaction Source from the daily transaction, Transaction Description from the daily transaction, Transaction Amount from the daily transaction, Merchant ID from the daily transaction, Merchant Name from the daily transaction, Merchant City from the daily transaction, Merchant ZIP Code from the daily transaction, Card Number from the daily transaction, and Original Transaction Timestamp from the daily transaction — all fields must be present and correctly mapped before the write is attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction Record with All Required Fields Before Posting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before a validated transaction can be permanently recorded, all relevant fields from the daily transaction input must be mapped into the transaction record, including transaction identity, merchant details, card number, and timestamps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A validated transaction is being prepared for posting to the Transaction Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system generates the processing timestamp for the transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time must be captured at the moment of posting and formatted as a standard timestamp containing: 4-digit Year, 2-digit Month, 2-digit Day, 2-digit Hour, 2-digit Minute, 2-digit Second, and Milliseconds — this processing timestamp must be stored in the Transaction Processing Timestamp field of the transaction record, and is distinct from the Original Transaction Timestamp which reflects when the transaction originally occurred

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture System Processing Timestamp at Time of Posting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each posted transaction must carry a processing timestamp that reflects the exact system date and time at which the transaction was posted, providing an audit trail distinct from the original transaction timestamp.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been fully populated with all required fields including Transaction ID, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Source, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant ZIP Code, Card Number, Original Transaction Timestamp, and Processing Timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the transaction record to the Transaction Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record must be successfully written to the Transaction Master file as a permanent record of the posted transaction, and processing must continue to the next transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Fully Populated Transaction Record to Transaction Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a transaction record is fully populated with all transaction details and the processing timestamp, it must be written to the Transaction Master file to create a permanent record of the posted transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fully populated transaction record has been submitted for writing to the Transaction Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation to the Transaction Master file does not complete successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately halt all transaction processing — no further transactions may be read, validated, or posted — and the failure must be reported as a critical error indicating that the Transaction Master file write operation failed, ensuring no partial or inconsistent data is left in an indeterminate state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Halt All Processing When Transaction Write to Master File Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system is unable to write a validated and fully populated transaction record to the Transaction Master file, this represents a critical failure that prevents further processing. All transaction processing must be immediately halted to protect data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A validated transaction record containing all required fields — Transaction ID, Transaction Type Code, Transaction Category Code, Transaction Source, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant ZIP Code, Card Number, Original Transaction Timestamp, and Processing Timestamp — has been submitted for writing to the Transaction Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation to the Transaction Master file completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction is considered permanently posted and recorded in the Transaction Master file, the posting process for that transaction is complete, and the system proceeds to process the next available daily transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction is Permanently Posted Upon Successful Write
all_rules.Rule_Description: A transaction is only considered fully and permanently posted once it has been successfully written to the Transaction Master file. Successful completion of the write operation marks the end of the posting lifecycle for that transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The daily transaction processing loop has completed and the end-of-file condition has been reached on the Daily Transaction Input File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program exits the transaction processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All six files must be closed in the following order: (1) Daily Transaction Input File, (2) Transaction Master Output File, (3) Card-to-Account Cross Reference File, (4) Daily Rejects Output File, (5) Account Master File, (6) Transaction Category Balance File — and processing continues to the summary reporting step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close All Processing Files After Transaction Loop Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all daily transactions have been read and processed (end of input file reached), all six files used during processing must be closed in sequence before any reporting or program termination occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All processing files have been successfully closed after the transaction processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the summary reporting step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :' followed by the value of the total transaction counter (WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT), representing every transaction record that was read from the Daily Transaction Input File during the run

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Total Transactions Processed Count
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all files are closed, the program must display the total number of daily transactions that were read and processed during the execution run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All processing files have been successfully closed after the transaction processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the summary reporting step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :' followed by the value of the rejection counter (WS-REJECT-COUNT), representing every transaction that failed one or more validation checks and was written to the Daily Rejects Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Total Transactions Rejected Count
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all files are closed, the program must display the total number of daily transactions that failed validation and were written to the Daily Rejects Output File during the execution run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The summary report has been displayed showing total transactions processed and total transactions rejected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total rejected transaction count (WS-REJECT-COUNT) is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program sets the Return Code to 4 to signal to the calling process that the run completed with partial success — meaning some transactions were rejected and written to the Daily Rejects Output File — requiring downstream review and intervention

all_rules.Rule_Name: Signal Partial Completion When Rejected Transactions Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: After displaying the summary report, the program evaluates whether any transactions were rejected during processing. If rejections occurred, the program must signal partial completion to the calling process by setting a specific return code, indicating that not all transactions were successfully posted and manual review of the rejects file is required.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The summary report has been displayed showing total transactions processed and total transactions rejected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total rejected transaction count (WS-REJECT-COUNT) is equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program does not set any special return code and terminates normally, signaling to the calling process that all transactions were successfully validated and posted with no exceptions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Normal Program Completion When No Transactions Were Rejected
all_rules.Rule_Description: If no transactions were rejected during the processing run, the program completes normally without setting any error return code, signaling to the calling process that all transactions were successfully validated and posted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All files have been closed, the summary report has been displayed, and the return code has been set if rejections occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All end-of-job steps have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN02C' and terminates, returning control to the calling process with either a return code of 4 (if rejections existed) or the default return code (if no rejections occurred)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Termination After Completion Signaling
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all files are closed, summary counts are displayed, and the appropriate return code is set (if applicable), the program must formally end execution and return control to the calling process.

description:
CBTRN02C is a batch COBOL program in the CardDemo application that reads daily credit card transactions from a sequential input file, validates each transaction (card number lookup, account existence, credit limit check, and account expiration check), and posts valid transactions to the transaction master file while writing rejected transactions with failure reasons to a daily rejects file. The program also updates the account balance and transaction category balance records for each successfully posted transaction. It is a standalone main/driver program with no CICS or MQ calls, operating against VSAM indexed and sequential files.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Sequential and Indexed Files) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Open all required files: Daily Transaction input file, Transaction master file (output), Card-to-Account Cross Reference file, Daily Rejects output file, Account Master file, and Transaction Category Balance file before processing begins. 2: Read Daily Transaction - Read the next transaction record sequentially from the Daily Transaction file and increment the transaction counter. 3: Reset Validation Status - Before validating each transaction, reset the validation failure reason code to zero and clear the failure reason description to prepare for fresh validation. 4: Validate Card Number via Cross Reference Lookup - Look up the card number from the transaction in the Card-to-Account Cross Reference file. If the card number is not found, mark the transaction as invalid with reason code 100 and description 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND'. 5: Validate Account Existence - Using the account ID retrieved from the cross reference, look up the account in the Account Master file. If the account is not found, mark the transaction as invalid with reason code 101 and description 'ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND'. 6: Validate Credit Limit - Calculate a temporary balance by adding the transaction amount to the current cycle credits minus current cycle debits. If this balance exceeds the account credit limit, mark the transaction as invalid with reason code 102 and description 'OVERLIMIT TRANSACTION'. 7: Validate Account Expiration Date - Compare the account expiration date against the transaction origination date. If the account has expired before the transaction date, mark the transaction as invalid with reason code 103 and description 'TRANSACTION RECEIVED AFTER ACCT EXPIRATION'. 8: Write Rejected Transaction - For transactions that fail validation, write the original transaction data along with the validation failure reason code and description to the Daily Rejects output file, and increment the reject counter. 9: Prepare Transaction Record for Posting - For valid transactions, map all transaction fields (ID, type code, category code, source, description, amount, merchant details, card number, origination timestamp) from the daily transaction record to the transaction master record structure. 10: Generate Processing Timestamp - Capture the current system date and time and format it as a standard timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mmm0000) to record when the transaction was processed. 11: Update Transaction Category Balance - Look up the transaction category balance record using the account ID, transaction type code, and transaction category code as a composite key. If the record exists, add the transaction amount to the existing category balance. If the record does not exist, create a new category balance record initialized with the transaction amount. 12: Update Account Balances - Add the transaction amount to the account's current balance. If the transaction amount is positive (credit), add it to the current cycle credit total. If the transaction amount is negative (debit), add it to the current cycle debit total. Save the updated account record back to the Account Master file. 13: Write Posted Transaction to Transaction Master - Write the fully populated transaction record to the Transaction Master file as a permanent record of the posted transaction. 14: Program Completion and Reporting - After processing all transactions, close all files, display the total count of transactions processed and the count of rejected transactions. If any transactions were rejected, set the return code to 4 to signal partial completion to the calling process.
